edition.locus: Eusebius HE 5.1.33-36 (God's dispensation; joy against conscience)

source_text: Ἐνταῦθα δὴ μεγάλη τις οἰκονομία θεοῦ ἐγίνετο καὶ ἔλεος ἀμέτρητον ἀνεφαίνετο Ἰησοῦ, σπανίως μὲν ἐν τῇ ἀδελφότητι γεγονός, μὴ ἀπολειπόμενον δὲ τῆς τέχνης Χριστοῦ. Οἱ γὰρ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην σύλληψιν ἔξαρνοι γενόμενοι συνεχλείοντο καὶ αὐτοὶ καὶ μετεῖχον τῶν δεινῶν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ ὄφελός τι αὐτοῖς ἡ ἐξάρνησις ἐγίνετο, ἀλλ᾽ οἱ μὲν ὁμολογοῦντες ὃ καὶ ἦσαν, συνεκλείοντο ὡς Χριστιανοί, μηδεμιᾶς ἄλλης αἰτίας αὐτοῖς ἐπιφερομένης, οὗτοι δὲ λοιπὸν ὡς ἀνδροφόνοι καὶ μιαροὶ κατείχοντο, διττότερον παρὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς κολαζόμενοι. Ἐκείνους μὲν γὰρ ἐπεκούφιζεν ἡ χαρὰ τῆς μαρτυρίας καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων καὶ ἡ πρὸς τὸν Χριστὸν ἀγάπη καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πατρικόν, τούτους δὲ τὸ συνειδὸς μεγάλως ἐτιμωρεῖτο, ὥστε καὶ παρὰ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἅπασιν κατὰ τὰς παρόδους διαδήλους τὰς ὄψεις αὐτῶν εἶναι. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἱλαροὶ προῄεσαν, δόξης καὶ χάριτος πολλῆς ταῖς ὄψεσιν αὐτῶν συγκεκραμένης, ὥστε καὶ τὰ δεσμὰ κόσμον εὐπρεπῆ περικεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς, ὡς νύμφῃ κεκοσμημένῃ ἐν χρυσωτοῖς χρυσοῖς πεποικιλμένοις, τὴν εὐωδίαν ὀδωδότες ἅμα τὴν Χριστοῦ, ὥστε ἐνίους δόξαι καὶ μύρῳ κοσμικῷ κεχρῖσθαι αὐτούς· οἱ δὲ κατηφεῖς καὶ ταπεινοὶ καὶ δυσειδεῖς καὶ πάσης ἀσχημοσύνης ἀνάπλεοι, προσέτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ὀνειδιζόμενοι ὡς ἀγεννεῖς καὶ ἄνανδροι, ἀνδροφόνων μὲν ἐγκλήματα ἔχοντες, ἀπολωλεκότες δὲ τὴν πάντιμον καὶ ἔνδοξον καὶ ζωοποιὸν προσηγορίαν. Ταῦτα δὲ οἱ λοιποὶ θεωροῦντες ἐστηρίχθησαν, καὶ οἱ συλλαμβανόμενοι ἀδιστάκτως ὡμολόγουν, μηδὲ ἔννοιαν ἔχοντες διαβολικοῦ λογισμοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: Here then a certain great dispensation of God came to pass and immeasurable mercy of Jesus was manifested, having rarely come to be in the brotherhood, yet not falling short of the skill of Christ. For those who at the first arrest had become deniers were themselves also shut up together and shared in the dreadful things; for not even in this moment did the denial prove any benefit to them, but while on the one hand those confessing what they also were were shut up together as Christians, with no other cause laid against them, these on the other hand were henceforth held as murderers and defiled, being punished doubly beyond the rest. For the former the joy of the testimony and the hope of the promised things and the love toward Christ and the paternal spirit gave relief, but the latter conscience punished greatly, so that even to all the rest their faces were conspicuous in the passings by. For the one sort went forward cheerful, with much glory and grace mingled together in their faces, so that even the bonds lay about them as a comely ornament, as upon a bride adorned in gold-fringed golden things diversified with embroidery, having emitted at once the sweet savor of Christ, so that some thought that they had even been anointed with worldly ointment; but the other sort were downcast and humble and ill-favored and full of all unseemliness, and besides were also reproached by the Gentiles as base and unmanly, having charges of murderers, but having lost the all-honored and glorious and life-giving appellation. And the rest beholding these things were strengthened, and those being arrested confessed unhesitatingly, having not even a notion of a diabolical reckoning.
pass_b_english: Here, then, a great providence of God took place, and the boundless mercy of Jesus appeared — a thing that had rarely occurred among the brethren, yet it did not fall short of Christ's healing work. For those who had denied at the first arrest were shut up with the rest as well and came to share the hardships; their denial brought them no advantage even at this moment. While those who confessed what they truly were were imprisoned simply as Christians, with no other accusation laid against them, these others were henceforth detained as murderers and defiled men, and were punished twice as severely as the rest. The joy of witness, the hope of the promises, love toward Christ, and the Spirit of the Father eased the burden for the former, but conscience tormented the latter grievously, so that their faces were plain for all the rest to see as they passed by.

For the faithful went forward cheerful, with much glory and grace blended into their looks, so that even their chains rested upon them like a beautiful adornment, like that of a bride dressed in robes of gold embroidered work (Psalm 45:13-14), and they breathed out together the fragrance of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15), so that some supposed they had been anointed with costly perfume from this world. But the others were gloomy and humbled and unsightly and filled with every deformity, and besides they were taunted by the Gentiles as low-born and cowardly, bearing the charges of murderers, yet having lost the wholly honored and glorious and life-giving Name. When the rest saw this contrast they were made firm, and those who were arrested confessed without hesitation, entertaining not even a thought of the devil's cunning.

choices.why: subject of ἐγίνετο with ἔλεος; context is God bringing deniers back through re-imprisonment, so redemptive ordering rather than household management
genitive after ἀπολειπόμενον; paired with ἔλεος ἀμέτρητον and rare restoration in ἀδελφότητι, so art as physician's craft toward deniers
fourth subject of ἐπεκούφιζεν alongside joy, hope, love; article + adjective denotes divine Spirit promised to witnesses, not merely a filial attitude
